title: The Impact of Climate on the Caspian Sea Level: Fluctuations in the Past, Present, and Future
content:
The article considers the level of the Caspian Sea from the paleoperiod to the modern state. The article gives a perspective analysis of the level change under the conditions of modern climatic change. The historical level fluctuations were analyzed. The most reliable data on the range of fluctuations were obtained for the first and second millennia AD. During this period, archaeological and historical data were added to the traditional geochronological methods. In the 10th-13th centuries during the Derbent regression the level decreased to minus 33 meters, and in the middle of the 17th century the sea level rose to minus 22.5 meters. 
Reliable level measurements started to be carried out since 1900. From this period to the present, the Caspian Sea level has varied from minus 25.74 m BS to minus 29.01 m BS. The lowest level (minus 29.01 m BS) was observed in 1977. In 2023 the level maximally approached the lowest level for this period and amounted to minus 28.95 m BS. 
The Caspian Sea level is projected to continue to decline until 2055 and reach minus 34.17 m BS (under the RCP 8.5 climate scenario) and minus 32.59 m BS (under the RCP 4.5 climate scenario). It is important to note the fact that the minimum level projected for 2055 has already been observed in the history of Caspian Sea level changes.
